messages:
maria_s: Hey team — customer ACME Corp hitting sustained 429s on our Dedicated pool after yesterday's plan-sync. Seeing spike starting ~10:40 UTC.
kevin_ops: Which pool and tenant id?
maria_s: dedicated-eu-west-1/pool-03, tenant acme-corp (tenant_id=t-acme). Logs show per-tenant throttle checks returning quota_exceeded.
sam_support: Customer says they didn't change usage. Billing plan migration completed last night.
kevin_ops: hmmm. I pulled rateprofile for t-acme: "units": 600, "period": "minute". But our dedicated rate adapter expects "requests_per_minute" mapping; there's a legacy config that expects per-second units.
ryan_eng: That's suspicious — unit-systems mismatch. Can you paste the exact config snippet?
maria_s: ```json
{"tenant_id":"t-acme","quota_units":600,"quota_unit_type":"minute","burst_capacity":5}
```
oncall: deploy-bot: rollout/plan-sync completed 2026-02-20T22:38Z :white_check_mark: 
kevin_ops: I found code path: plan-sync payload used by dedicated-controller had an older key "quota_units_per_sec" fallback when unit_type missing. Plan migration omitted unit_type for migrated tenants, so controller interpreted 600 as per-second -> 36k rpm effectively, then our translator capped it incorrectly to 600 rps which converted to 36k rpm vs expected 600 rpm — result: system produced tight per-tenant buckets causing sudden throttles when autoscaler trimmed pool.
sam_support: TL;DR: a missing field in plan-migrate made quota adapter choose wrong conversion -> over-aggressive enforced limit? That sounds inverted.
kevin_ops: Exactly. Because translator saw units as per-sec, it created a token-bucket with capacity=600 tokens/sec but when we merged with our per-minute enforcement layer it applied a floor that caused burst tokens to be smaller after recent autoscale changes. Combined with noisy neighbor, acme got frequent 429s.
maria_s: Repro steps I ran:
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <ACME_KEY>" https://dedicated.eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":32}' -v
2) watch tail -n 200 /var/log/dedicated/pool-03/throttle.log | grep t-acme
Logs show repeated:
"throttle check: tenant=t-acme limit=600 period=minute tokens_left=0 -> 429"
ryan_eng: Can you share metrics screenshot? I see autoscaler event at 22:39 that reduced pods from 8->5 due to CPU signal.
maria_s: attaching small CSV of qps per tenant (pasted inline):
"ts,qps_total,qps_t-acme,qps_top2"
"22:35",1200,300,560
"22:40",900,320,480
"22:45",700,310,360
kevin_ops: Action plan:
- short term: increase per-tenant soft limit for t-acme to 5x until fix (owner: kevin_ops) :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
- mid term: patch plan-migrate to always include unit_type; add migration audit (owner: ryan_eng)
- infra: change autoscaler to account for burst tokens in dedicated pool math (owner: eng-runtime)
sam_support: I notified customer and opened ticket with workaround key rotation. They're fine with temporary increase.
maria_s: I'll apply the soft bump now and monitor. /cc @ryan_eng @kevin_ops
kevin_ops: done — bumped soft_limit to 3000 rpm for t-acme, restoring success rate. Monitoring: 200 -> 95% success within 3m :rocket: 
oncall: Note: filed incident INC-2026-0422 for postmortem. tagging for ops review :memo: 
ryan_eng: I'll own the migration patch. Will PR today and add unit test for unit_type presence.
maria_s: Thanks all. Will keep this thread updated if anything regresses.
